draft.title: Humanism
card: Humanism was an idea that grew during the Renaissance. Humanists studied the texts of ancient Greece and Rome, such as works on history, poetry and ethics (ideas about right and wrong).
Humanists believed people could improve themselves through learning. They valued education in subjects such as grammar, history and philosophy.
Medieval thinkers had often focused on preparing for the next life. Humanists paid more attention to life on Earth and to what people could achieve.
Many humanists were still religious Christians. They did not reject religion. They gave human thought and achievement more attention.
draft.remember: Humanists used ancient learning to improve people and valued human achievement in this life.

a.q: Which belief was most typical of a Renaissance humanist?
opts: Education can help people improve themselves
People should give up learning to focus on faith
Ancient texts were wrong and should be ignored
Only nobles could gain anything from education
a.why: Humanists believed learning could improve people. The option about giving up learning is tempting, but humanists valued study and many stayed religious.
a.clue: Think about what humanists thought learning could do for a person.

b.q: Marco, a scholar in Venice in the 1400s, studies Roman poetry and history and praises what people can achieve. What does this show about him?
opts: He is a humanist who gives attention to human achievement
He has rejected religion and no longer believes in God
He follows the medieval focus on preparing for the next life
He is copying ancient art rather than studying ancient texts
b.why: Studying ancient texts and praising human achievement are signs of humanism. It is wrong to say he rejected religion, because the card says many humanists were still religious Christians.
b.clue: Humanists could study ancient texts and still be religious.

a.best: Education can help people improve themselves

b.best: He is a humanist who gives attention to human achievement
